core_meaning.short_meaning: My servant; Arabic form with East African use
core_meaning.primary_meaning: Abdi represents Arabic عَبْدِي (ʿabdī), literally “my servant”; it is also a common personal-name form in Somali and other Horn of Africa contexts.
core_meaning.literal_meaning: The name is the Arabic word itself, used unchanged as a given name rather than a derived or diminutive form.
core_meaning.meaning_explanation: The Arabic form عَبْدِي combines عبد (“servant”) with the first-person possessive suffix ـي (“my”). It does not literally contain الله (“God”), so “my servant of God” is an interpretive expansion. Abdi is also established in Somali/East African naming.

etymology.etymology_explanation: The form عَبْدِي is built from عبد and the possessive suffix ـي. It is used as a personal name, including in Somali/East African contexts.

faq.a: Abdi represents Arabic عَبْدِي (ʿabdī), literally “my servant”; the phrase “of God” is not literally present.

faq.q: What is the origin of Abdi?
faq.a: The form is Arabic in structure and is also widely used in Somali/East African naming contexts.
Yes. The underlying Arabic form recorded here is عَبْدِي (ʿabdī).

faq.q: What is the root of Abdi?
faq.a: It combines عبد (“servant”) with the first-person possessive suffix ـي (“my”).
Abdi is used by Muslims, including in Somali/East African communities, but its literal meaning is “my servant,” not a complete phrase “servant of God.”
This record does not establish Abdi as an explicitly named Qur'anic person; Arabic origin and Muslim use are not sufficient proof of personal-name attestation.

faq.q: What does Abdi mean in Urdu?
faq.a: In Urdu, عبدی can be read as “میرا بندہ”; the addition “اللہ کا” is not literal in the form.
The supplied “ab-di” is an approximate pronunciation of عَبْدِي.

faq.q: Is Abdi a boy's or girl's name?
faq.a: The record classifies Abdi as masculine in common use, but naming conventions can vary across communities.
